newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIAN STRIKER KANU HAS HEART SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIAN STRIKER KANU HAS HEART SURGERY.

text.p: Nigerian striker Nwankwo Kanu has successfully undergone surgery at a U.S. hospital to correct a heart defect which threatened his soccer career, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reported on Thursday.

Nigerian consular officer in the United States, Sunmonu Bello-Osagie, who has accompanied Kanu since he arrived in the U.S. last weekend for surgery said the operation at Cleveland Hospital in Ohio lasted four hours and everything had gone well.
He quoted Kanu as saying "I will be back" and giving the 'V' for victory sign as he was wheeled into the theatre for surgery.
Kanu is sentimental favourite to be named African Footballer of the Year this weekend despite his playing career coming to an abrupt end because of the detection of the heart problem.

The 20-year-old Kanu captained Nigeria's under-23 team to the gold medal at the Atlanta Olympics but was sidelined soon after when doctors dicovered a heart defect that threatened to kill him if he continued playing.

His crucial goals for Nigeria at the Olympics, combined with a sympathy vote from the Confederation of African Football's panel, is expected to see him become the third Nigerian in four years to win the award.
The award will be announced in Cairo this weekend.

Kanu's heart condition was discovered during a routine medical examination at the Italian Institute of Sports Medicine after his transfer from Dutch club Ajax Amsterdam, where he won a European Cup winners' medal, to Internazionale of Italy.
NAN said the doctors who performed the operation would issue a statement at the weekend on Kanu's condition.
He was expected to recover fully within eight weeks, it added.
